g.text: Ethernet TAS (IEEE 802.1Qbv Time-Aware Shaper) Example Project
[Until both ETH0 and ETH1 UP (timeout 5 s)]
console: "[TAS] ETH0 link: UP ETH1 link: UP (after N ms)"
Standalone mode: ESWM local free-running timer,
clock_period is the ns/tick written to PTPTIVC0.TIV
-- must equal the ESWM timer's real clock period
(5 on this board; 4 was 5/4 too slow -> 31.25 ms cycle)
[Repeat forever -- no separate "stop" step to leave this loop]
Apply Schedule for Selected Use Case
Drop entries left over from previous use case
Program 25 ms cycle, Q0-Q3 5 ms windows, Q4-Q7 closed
(UC1: Port1 only, UC2: CPU port only, UC3: both ORed)
cycle_time / gate entry counts / MAC table entries
One independent descriptor queue per TAS queue
CreateDescriptorQueue() keeps the address of s_tx_queue_cfg[q],
so that cfg struct is static, not a stack temporary.
Idempotent per queue (s_tx_queue_created[q]) -- safe on a use-case switch.
console: "[TAS] Injecting one frame per open queue every cycle."
console: "[TAS] Waiting for external traffic on Port 1."
console: "Type a different use case number (1-3) any time to switch..."
Run Loop (until a different use case is selected)
[For each row with CPU_PORT in source_port_mask (ascending window offset)]
windows[0].offset_ns (static table value, no timer read)
Frame buffered in that queue until
this queue still pending because its gate hasn't opened)
-> retry StartDescriptorQueue, treat as a skip, non-fatal
Buffered until that queue's gate opens
Gated egress on ETH0 -- 1 frame per open queue
per cycle, clustered inside its 5 ms window
TAS buffers a frame that arrives before its gate opens
-- it does not drop it. A single frame only proves
MAC-table steering; the continuous per-cycle pattern
(A) packet capture on ETH0 (I/O Graph + per-queue window
table); (B) oscilloscope on the ESWM_TASGATE0_x pins
(25 ms cycle / 5 ms window, all 4 queues). In modes 1/3
the capture shows a run-to-run beat between the PC
script's clock and the board's -- not a gate defect.
console: "[TAS] Use case N is already active."
